system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Nvidia (NVDA) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: NVIDIA -2.8% gapped higher following its impressive earnings report last night, but has pulled back into negative territory

BODY:
[No article body - headline only]
</article>

<summary>
Nvidia (NVDA) shares initially gapped higher after the company posted a strong earnings report, reflecting positive market reaction to the results. However, the stock has since reversed course and is now trading down approximately 2.8% on the day, erasing the earlier gains. This pullback suggests investors may be taking profits or reassessing valuation despite the earnings beat, or broader market/sector pressures could be weighing on the stock. Investors should watch for further details on guidance, margins, or sector sentiment that may clarify the reversal despite the initially well-received earnings report.
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article. For each give:
  type: "outside_fact" (a fact, number or date not in the article), "wrong_detail" (contradicts the article:
        number, direction, entity, date), "unattributed" (a sourced or rumoured report stated as fact),
        "speculation" (an opinion, implication or forecast the article does not make, incl. links to NVDA)
  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about NVDA in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a NVDA analyst what matters, and represent how central NVDA really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for NVDA, and says so plainly if NVDA is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the NVDA angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores NVDA, or implies the article is about / important for NVDA when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": [{"claim": "...", "type": "outside_fact" | "wrong_detail" | "unattributed" | "speculation", "severity": "material" | "minor"}],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
